page.layout: One page of text, with a running head above and a catchword below the last line on the right. A narrow strip of the facing left page, cut off at the gutter, runs down the left edge and is not transcribed.

main_text.l: [?]quod[?] nos, idque feriò, & quò pejores dies sunt,
[?]ectione caveamus greffibus noftris. Ne à recto
[?]nive illecebris ad dextram siniftramve vel tantil-
[?]ecerimus mala, nullum vel apud Deum judicem [?]vel
apud testem Conscientiam, habitura esse in illo
[?]ie excusationem. Et de bonæ intentionis prætextu

page.notes: The left edge of the text is clipped by the gutter shadow, so the first letter of several lines is doubtful and marked [?]; the words are reconstructed from the visible letters. The Greek word after "eò" is only partly legible; the form is doubtful and marked [?]. The strip at the left belongs to the facing page and is not transcribed. "Præleätione" at the end is partly overprinted by a dark mark. The large bold "PRÆ-" and a dark blot near the lower middle are a catchword and stain, the stain being left out. The heading and the top text carry no further marks.
